text: Independent evidence from multiple Earth-observation sources corroborates the 2021 tree-cover loss claim for this asset. The Hansen Global Forest Change dataset (GFC-2025-v1.13) detected **81.3 hectares (2.23% of the asset) of tree-cover loss** in 2021. This was cross-verified by the **JRC Global Forest Cover 2020 (GFC2020) dataset**, which confirmed that **98% of the affected area** was forested in 2020, supporting the validity of the loss event. Additionally, Uruguay’s MGAP 2021 forest map identified the affected area as **planted forest (68.1 ha of Pinus spp.)**, with no native forest loss detected. The evidence is further strengthened by the observability of the event in later years (up to 2025) and the consistency across datasets. However, the cause (e.g., harvesting, fire) or legality of the loss remains undetermined.
